text_blocks.snippet: IL-17 drugs, also known as Interleukin-17 (IL-17) inhibitors, are a class of medications used to treat autoimmune and inflammatory conditions. They work by blocking the action of IL-17, a protein that plays a role in inflammation. Commonly prescribed IL-17 inhibitors include secukinumab (Cosentyx), ixekizumab (Taltz), and brodalumab (Siliq).
snippet_highlighted_words: a class of medications used to treat autoimmune and inflammatory conditions

list.snippet: IL-17 inhibitors are biologic drugs that target the IL-17 pathway, a key part of the inflammatory process.
They are typically monoclonal antibodies, meaning they are designed to bind to a specific target (in this case, IL-17 or its receptor) and block its activity.

text_blocks.snippet: What conditions are they used to treat?

list.title: Psoriasis:
list.snippet: IL-17 inhibitors are a first-line treatment option for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis.

list.title: Psoriatic Arthritis:
list.snippet: They are also used to manage psoriatic arthritis, a condition that affects both the skin and joints.

list.title: Ankylosing Spondylitis:
list.snippet: Some IL-17 inhibitors, like secukinumab and ixekizumab, are approved for treating ankylosing spondylitis, a form of inflammatory arthritis that primarily affects the spine.

list.title: Hidradenitis Suppurativa:
list.snippet: Secukinumab is also approved for treating hidradenitis suppurativa, a chronic inflammatory skin condition.
Secukinumab (Cosentyx): A fully humanized IgG1κ monoclonal antibody that selectively inhibits IL-17A.
Ixekizumab (Taltz): A humanized IgG4 monoclonal antibody that also targets IL-17A.
Brodalumab (Siliq): A human monoclonal antibody that binds to the IL-17 receptor A.
Bimekizumab (Bimzelx): Another IL-17 inhibitor that is currently in clinical trials for various conditions.

list.title: Side Effects:
list.snippet: IL-17 inhibitors can increase the risk of infections, particularly respiratory infections and candidiasis (yeast infections). They may also be associated with an increased risk of inflammatory bowel disease.

list.title: Paradoxical Effects:
list.snippet: In some cases, IL-17 inhibitors have been associated with paradoxical effects, such as disease exacerbation in individuals with inflammatory bowel disease.

list.title: Long-term Safety:
list.snippet: The long-term safety of IL-17 inhibitors is still being studied, and ongoing research is important to understand the full scope of their effects.

text_blocks.snippet: IL-17 medications, also known as IL-17 inhibitors, are a class of biologic drugs used to treat autoimmune diseases by targeting the interleukin-17 (IL-17) pathway, a key player in inflammation. These medications are primarily used for conditions like psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, and ankylosing spondylitis.
snippet_highlighted_words: a class of biologic drugs used to treat autoimmune diseases by targeting the interleukin-17 (IL-17) pathway

text_blocks.snippet: How they work: IL-17 inhibitors block the action of IL-17 proteins, which are involved in the inflammatory process. By inhibiting these proteins, the medications help reduce inflammation and improve symptoms associated with these conditions.

list.snippet: Secukinumab (Cosentyx): A fully humanized monoclonal antibody that inhibits IL-17A.
Ixekizumab (Taltz): A humanized monoclonal antibody that also targets IL-17A.
Brodalumab (Siliq): Targets the IL-17 receptor, blocking its interaction with IL-17.
Bimekizumab (Bimzelx): A monoclonal antibody that inhibits both IL-17A and IL-17F.
Plaque psoriasis: All four of the above-mentioned medications are FDA-approved for plaque psoriasis.
Psoriatic arthritis: Secukinumab, ixekizumab, and brodalumab are also approved for psoriatic arthritis.
Ankylosing spondylitis: Secukinumab and ixekizumab are used to treat ankylosing spondylitis.

list.title: Paradoxical effects:
list.snippet: IL-17 inhibitors can sometimes cause paradoxical effects, such as the exacerbation or new onset of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD).

list.title: Potential for infection:
list.snippet: As with other biologics, IL-17 inhibitors can increase the risk of infections.

list.title: Consultation with a healthcare professional:
list.snippet: It's crucial to consult with a doctor or rheumatologist to determine if an IL-17 inhibitor is the right treatment option and to discuss potential risks and benefits, according to Alberta Rheumatology.
